Also government issued 2024 immigration/asylum protections for LGBTQ people. But those are resident-facing.

Hmm, but rule 1: resident-facing machinery is climate signal at most. Still, it's a directly documented positive about institutions (a court/tribunal granting protection on gender identity grounds) — that's a climate signal of some institutional recognition, above states where nothing.

So there is: documented police targeting of trans people at identity checks (a traveler-relevant axis: ID checks are exactly a traveler exposure), plus no remedies, plus no anti-discrimination law, against institutional climate signals of some protection in asylum, plus no criminalisation and no facility bans documented.

Our dossier has no documented universal-exposure measure; the exposure is police encounters at identity checks, which is not universal-exposure-by-rule but happens to visibly trans people — analogous to 0.35-C. So 0.35 is right.
